title: Largest impact craters
measure: Estimated original diameter of the crater in km, for impact structures confirmed by the Earth Impact Database. Erosion has worn most of these down, so their original size is worked out from what's left, and estimates vary.

entries.name: Vredefort
entries.note: The oldest and largest known. Other studies put its original size at 250 to 300 km.
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA

entries.name: Chicxulub
entries.note: Buried under the Yucatán. The impact that wiped out the dinosaurs, 66 million years ago.
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA

entries.name: Sudbury
entries.note: Home to one of the world's biggest nickel mines, made from the impact's melted rock.
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA

entries.name: Popigai
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA

entries.name: Acraman
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA

entries.name: Manicouagan
entries.note: Now a ring-shaped lake, and one of the best preserved large craters. Some sources give 100 km.
entries.source: Earth Impact Database (Planetary and Space Science Centre, University of New Brunswick), via NASA
